title: Posted Notice at the Licensed Facility: Commodity Checkoff and Capital Retain on Grain Marketing Contracts
content:
Two withholdings attach to every settlement of patronage-eligible bushels under Grain Marketing Contracts and are shown as their own lines.

**The checkoff.** The statutory commodity checkoff is withheld at the published rate on the settled bushels, and exactly one checkoff line is carried on a settlement statement, so a corrected statement adjusts the existing line rather than adding a second. The line is correlated to the statement by its settlement number, and what distinguishes one line from another is the day it was posted and the amount it carries. The checkoff line comes to the settled bushels multiplied by the published checkoff rate per bushel, rounded to the cent.

**Asking for the checkoff back.** The checkoff is refundable on request where the commodity's programme allows it, and a member who asks for the checkoff back does so no later than the refund window running from the day the settlement statement was issued. The refund window is counted in whole calendar days from the settlement date, the settlement date itself counting as day zero, and a request arriving on the final day of the window is still in time. A request after that is out of time and the desk has no discretion to take it.

*Boundary.* Where the published refund window is 45 calendar days, a request reaching the desk on the forty-fifth day after the settlement date, that date counting as day zero, is in time. A request reaching the desk on the forty-sixth day is out of time, and nothing in this notice allows it to be taken.

**Programmes outside patronage.** On a programme that is not patronage-eligible neither the retain nor any patronage allocation arises, and only the checkoff is withheld.

## Clause no longer in force

One clause of this notice is **no longer in force** and is carried here only so that no reader applies it:

> "The per-unit capital retain is withheld at the same time on programmes the catalogue marks as patronage-eligible, but it is not a charge: it is credited to the member's equity account and comes back to them on the board's revolvement cycle, so it is never refunded on request and never waived."
